findings.title: appStore entries are now un-awaited Promises, so consumers that index without await get a Promise object
findings.body: The appStore object was changed from namespace imports to `import(...)` promises. Every consumer that reads `appStore[key]` and then checks `"lib" in app` or `"CalendarService" in app.lib` without awaiting will now get a Promise, where `"lib" in promise` is false, so the app is silently treated as not implemented. Any call site not updated in this diff (e.g. other files using appStore, getApps-related code, or the `as keyof typeof appStore` lookups) will break silently at runtime rather than fail at compile time, since the types still look plausible.

findings.title: Lookup via appStore uses a dynamic import that can reject; error is not handled and the function now returns a rejected promise
findings.body: `await appStore[...]` now performs a dynamic import. If the key is unknown, `appStore[key]` is undefined and awaiting it yields undefined (handled), but if the module fails to load (missing module, build error) the rejection propagates out of getCalendar and every caller, which previously returned null gracefully. This changes failure behavior for calendar lookup.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials still calls getCalendar synchronously, now receiving a Promise
findings.body: getCalendarCredentials maps credentials with `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without await. getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` is a Promise stored in the returned array. getConnectedCalendars later does `await item.calendar`, but any other consumer of this function (and the type of the result) now deals with Promises, and the function itself is still synchronous so the calendar is created outside the await chain. Its errors also become unhandled promise rejections.

findings.title: forEach with async callback discards promises; deletion errors and completion are not awaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` does not await the async callbacks. The surrounding try/catch can no longer catch errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent (they become unhandled rejections), and the function returns true before calendar/video cancellations finish, so the reschedule can complete while the old events still exist.

findings.title: forEach with async callback discards promises; cancellation errors become unhandled
findings.body: Same issue as the vital variant: the async forEach callback is not awaited, so the try/catch no longer catches calendar/video delete failures and they surface as unhandled promise rejections, while the function proceeds to send emails and return true before deletions complete.

findings.title: forEach with async callback in requestReschedule; deletions not awaited and errors unhandled
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` fires calendar and video deletions without awaiting them. Errors become unhandled rejections (possibly crashing or spamming logs), and the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks while the previous calendar events may still be being deleted.

findings.title: forEach with async callback inside recurring cancellation; apiDeletes is read before pushes happen
findings.body: `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` is not awaited. `await apiDeletes` / `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs before these async pushes occur, so recurring-event calendar deletions are neither awaited nor guaranteed to complete before the booking is reported cancelled, and failures are unhandled.

findings.title: getCachedResults filters out nulls only after mapping, relying on index alignment that may now be wrong
findings.body: Calendars are resolved with Promise.all over calendarCredentials, preserving order, so index matching still works, but the comment about nulls is now misleading and the resolved calendars are not paired with credentials after any filtering. Low risk on its own, but combined with other un-awaited uses it is fragile.

findings.title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not the pending deletions
findings.body: `await apiDeletes;` on an array does not wait for any of the contained promises. The payment-rejection path therefore no longer waits for calendar/video deletions before returning success, which is the pre-existing bug, but the async conversion of getCalendar makes the pushed promises even more likely to be missing from this array.

findings.title: Payment app lookup returns null from a function whose result is not a payment response; wrong type on fallback
findings.body: In the refund path, when the payment app is not implemented the handler does `return null` from within handler, which is not a valid cancel response and skips cancellation entirely after the booking has already been deemed to need refund handling. This was pre-existing but is now reached more often because the async lookup changes what the check sees.
